[F003] $ python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_canonical_discovery_f003.py -q

All 40 tests pass (38 prior + 2 new regression tests).

I addressed the single medium/correctness finding from the prior round (the `suggested_name` collision-safety gap in `canonical_discovery.py:347`). Previously `derive_suggested_name` appended `-<canonical_repo_key[:8]>` and returned that candidate unconditionally — so when both the base (`dontpanic`) and the hash-suffixed fallback (`dontpanic-abcdef12`) were already in `taken`, it returned a duplicate. I rewrote the collision path to build a deterministic, increasingly-specific suffix sequence: first the canonical-key hash at growing widths (`[:8]`, `[:12]`, `[:16]`, full key), then a numeric disambiguator `-<key[:8]>-<n>` over `range(1, len(taken)+2)`. The loop returns the first candidate that both matches `PROJECT_NAME_PATTERN` and is not in `taken`; the numeric tail provides `len(taken)+1` distinct candidates, which by pigeonhole guarantees at least one is free, so the function is now provably unique against any finite `taken` set while staying regex-safe and ≤64 chars. I added two regression tests: `test_suggested_name_collision_when_hash_suffix_also_taken` (reproduces the auditor's exact `{"dontpanic","dontpanic-abcdef12"}` case) and `test_suggested_name_unique_against_dense_collision_set` (exhausts the base plus all hash widths plus early numeric suffixes to exercise the disambiguator).
